history.period: Antiquity unverified; 17th-century origin claimed in online accounts
history.summary: A well-known Ganesha shrine on Bada Ganesh Road, Sumul Dairy Road, Katargam, housing a large marble idol of Lord Ganesha (hence 'Bada Ganesh'). The temple is a centre of festivities during Ganesh Chaturthi, celebrated with great enthusiasm. Local online accounts describe the temple as centuries old, with one video account claiming a 17th-century establishment 'during the reign of Siddhi Johar, a local prince' - this is DUBIOUS and unsourced (Siddhi Johar was a 17th-century Bijapur general, not a Surat prince). No reliable founding date or history could be established; treat the 17th-century claim as unverified. The temple is built in a traditional Gujarati style and also goes locally by the name Sardar Patel Ganesh Temple (per the same account).

name: Bada Ganesh Temple, Surat
town_description: Surat is a major city in Gujarat on the banks of the Tapi River, historically one of India's most important ports under Mughal and then British rule. Today it is a thriving metropolis known worldwide as a diamond-processing and textile-manufacturing hub. The city grew from a 12th-century settlement into a Mughal port and later a British stronghold, retaining colonial-era landmarks, old-city bazaars, and a fast-developing riverfront. It is well connected by air, rail, and road to Mumbai, Vadodara, and the rest of Gujarat.

travel.railway: Gaushala railway station ~0.7 km; Surat railway station ~5 km (verify)
travel.road: Bada Ganesh Road, Sumul Dairy Road, New Pushpakunj Society, Katargam; reachable by city bus and auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ganesh Chaturthi (August/September) is the grandest time (verify)
